questions.question: Let $N$ be a nonnegative integer-valued total, and let $X$ count labelled items. Suppose $X\mid N=n\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,p)$ for every possible $n$, with a fixed $0<p<1$. Which interpretation is justified by this count-level assumption?
options: Given the total $n$, the labelled count is fixed at its mean $np$, with no randomness left
The labelling probability $p$ may differ between different positive totals of items
Independent labelling with probability $p$ is one construction of the stated count law
The count law determines which particular items in the item order receive labels

questions.question: Let $N\sim\operatorname{Pois}(\lambda)$ with $\lambda>0$ and $X\mid N=n\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,p)$ for every nonnegative integer $n$, where $0<p<1$ and $q=1-p$. In the total-variance identity $\operatorname{Var}(X)=\mathbb{E}[\operatorname{Var}(X\mid N)]+\operatorname{Var}(\mathbb{E}[X\mid N])$, what are the first and second terms, respectively?

Let $N$ be a nonnegative integer-valued total with finite variance, mean $\mu>0$ and variance $v$. Suppose $X\mid N=n\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,p)$ for every possible $n$, where $0<p<1$, and set $Y=N-X$. Using $\operatorname{Cov}(X,Y)=\mathbb{E}[\operatorname{Cov}(X,Y\mid N)]+\operatorname{Cov}(\mathbb{E}[X\mid N],\mathbb{E}[Y\mid N])$, which conclusion is valid?
options: $\operatorname{Cov}(X,Y)=p(1-p)(v+\mu)$; a Poisson total therefore gives covariance $2\lambda p(1-p)>0$
$\operatorname{Cov}(X,Y)=-\mu p(1-p)$; only the mean of the total enters, so a Poisson total gives negative covariance
$\operatorname{Cov}(X,Y)=p(1-p)(v-\mu)$; equality of mean and variance alone does not establish independence
$\operatorname{Cov}(X,Y)=0$ for every total law, since the binomial split alone removes all dependence

questions.question: Let $N\sim\operatorname{Pois}(10)$ and $X\mid N=n\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,0.3)$ for every nonnegative integer $n$. Set $Y=N-X$ and $D=X-Y=2X-N$. What are $\mathbb{E}[\operatorname{Var}(D\mid N)]$, $\operatorname{Var}(\mathbb{E}[D\mid N])$ and $\operatorname{Var}(D)$, respectively?
